channel.title: The Foundation in a post-America world
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "The Foundation in a post-America world" - Tale: The Foundation's Contingency for the collapse of the United States of America

item.title: Re: The Foundation in a post-America world
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the crit and the greenlight :)

The other components hinting at the situation is a really good idea. While originally this was all going to be the foundation planning for a hypothetical situation, this and some chats on irc has convinced me to instead place the comments while the federal collapse is ongoing and the foundation has to put this contingency in place, giving higher stakes and leaving room for a bit of refreshing world building elements between the walls of text. This should (hopefully) break up the monotony a bit more.

item.title: Re: The Foundation in a post-America world
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

So this looks good, coherent and most importantly, something I would want to read. There are trappings though, like you've said, that the entire doc will seem less like a Tale and more a long laundry list of things to do.

I like the short comment sections - I think you will need some personal voices and opinions in there to break the monotony. I do think you should consider other such components, e.g. short newscaster logs to show what's going on out there, an MTF escort log as they seek to transport a scp to a new location (and fail). Lastly, I know you said you don't want to go into detail about what caused the collapse, but you should hint at it throughout the article. The reader would still want to know, and if you provided clues, I think that would be sufficient.

Here's a greenlight. Coherently, the article has enough content to stand on its own. Thematically, these are interesting what-if scenarios that can be explored in detail. Best of luck and hope you manage to get a second greenlight!

item.title: The Foundation in a post-America world
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page type: Tale.

Genre: Speculative Internal Document.

Page layout: Internal contingency plan in the form of an essay detailing foundation response to the crisis, interspersed with dialogue between characters on the proposals.

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation's internal plan to deal with a collapse of the Federal Government's control over America into a multi-party civil war.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: After a short section on assumptions for the scenario (Government control over large portions of the country has been lost, insurrection is in multiple, decentralized factions all over the country, etc. The document itself won't be discussing the cause/partisanship in the conflict, both to keep the article apolitical and to make it as generalized of a contingency plan as possible), the document will describe the foundation's priorities and what actions should be taken towards them in this scenario, including (as a first idea of topics):

  • Transport of all safe/easily transportable items out of the country (if necessary)
  • Security and Safety of Location SCPs and other objects that cannot be transferred out of America
  • Dealing with the remnants of the UIU
  • Complex supply lines during large scale societal collapse including the failure of vital infrastructure
  • Diplomacy with Federal government to maintain neutrality and peace
  • Preservation of the veil and acquisition of objects with the collapse of centralized communication

Following each of these points, there will be a short comment section from several researchers taking place during an American federal collapse with various approving and dissenting opinions on the proposal now the hypothetical has to be put into action. This is to make sure the article does not feel final or absolute, as it is a contingency plan written not for any one situation at hand, and to break up the walls of text that essays are prone to.

These discussions will hint at what caused the collapse of federal authority/what’s going on in America at large (as it comes up naturally) to give the reader a sense of purpose from the piece and a feeling of urgency, but it will not be explicitly spelled out anywhere.

Hook: The Foundation is incredibly America-centric. Due to America's influence and incredible stability over the last 100 years, having a huge portion of Foundation sites in the USA has never been a problem. If that were to change, dealing with it would be a massive logistical problem that would require huge adaption by sites and operations both inside the US and worldwide.
